sentences.text:
Kamal Kishore Gupta And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2
Others on 6 December, 2022

Author: Gautam Chowdhary
Bench: Gautam Chowdhary
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 87
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 39481 of 2022
Applicant :- Kamal Kishore Gupta And 2 Others
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Rohan Gupta

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This application has been filed for quashing of the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 39149 of 2022 under Section 26 read with Section 51, 59 of Food Safety Standards Act, 2006 pending before learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Moradabad as well as to quash the summoning order dated 29.06.2022 passed in the aforesaid case.

On perusal of the record, the Court finds that the allegations made in the complaint disclose commission of a cognizable offence, on the basis whereof the summoning order has been passed against the applicants.

This Court in exercise of its power under section 482 Cr.P.C., is not required to assess the correctness of the allegation and the reliability of the evidence, the prayer to quash the summoning order and the consequential proceeding is rejected.
Kamal Kishore Gupta And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 6 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96023878/

entities.text: Kamal Kishore Gupta And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this stage, the learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants have so far not been arrested in the above case and the police is seeking to arrest the applicants and there may be coercive processes issued against the applicants by the court concerned therefore, some direction may be issued to the court concerned for consideration of the bail prayer of the applicants.

As the Apex Court in Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, decided on 07.10.2021) has already laid down guidelines for grant of bail, without fettering the discretion of the courts concerned and the statutory provisions governing consideration in grant of bail, no specific direction need be issued by this Court as it is expected that the court concerned will take into consideration the necessary guidelines already issued by the Apex court.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With the aforesaid observations, the application is disposed off.
